item.title: Lower-temperature bulk depolymerization of commercial polymethacrylates
item.headline: Turning acrylic plastic back into its molecular ingredients
item.summary: An additive helped recover 90% monomer yield from commercial blue Plexiglas in a roughly 5-gram experiment. Industrial feasibility remains untested.

evidence.question: Can existing acrylic polymers be chemically recycled at lower temperatures?
evidence.method: Heating controls, mass-loss measurements, spectroscopy, and vacuum distillation.

explainer.finding: Chain-breaking chemistry recovered the small molecules used to make acrylic plastic.
explainer.method: Researchers heated ground Plexiglas with TCNHPI at 230°C for four hours under vacuum, then checked the collected monomer by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
explainer.meaning: Imagine recovering ingredients from a colored acrylic sheet rather than just melting it into another shape. The additive helps start breaks along polymer chains.
explainer.limits: Polyacrylates broke down without regenerating monomer. Mixed-waste recycling, industrial costs, and environmental benefits were not established.
